maya: FYI saw a perf regression on canary for the v2 batching heuristic, looks like matmul kernel count exploded after the change. perfetto trace attached in the run artifacts.
aj: which batch cfg? the aggressive pack one?
maya: yes, configs/batching/aggressive.json — it's trying to merge sequences and then we end up with lots of tiny GEMMs plus repeated workspace allocs.
dmitri: can you paste the perfetto flame snippet?
maya: here — perfetto timeline snippet: ```
GPU: cublasLtMatmul (algo=11, ws=0B) -> cublasLtMatmul (algo=21, ws=512MB) -> cuLaunchKernel (matmul-shim) -> cublasLtMatmul (algo=37, ws=0B) -> repeated 120x in 2s
Observations: alternating algo choices, many workspace-heavy launches causing fragmentation/alloc churn. KV cache hits unchanged.
```
sarah: interesting — algo 21 requires workspace; when workspace not reserved it triggers deviceAlloc per-call which fragments the allocator. Did nsys show mallocs?
maya: nsys summary: "cudaMalloc 1.1k calls, total 520MB, avg 430B" and a large tail. Also we see a lot of small matmuls (~64x128) happening because batch packing changed sequence grouping.
dmitri: sounds like two orthogonal regressions: batching now produces more small GEMMs, and kernel selector is picking a workspace-reliant algo for those sizes. We should prefer workspace-free algos for small shapes.
aj: can we reproduce quickly with the micro-bench? run: `tools/prof/micro_run.py --shape 64 128 512 --algo-scan --trace perfetto --cfg configs/batching/aggressive.json`
maya: ran that, attached `perfetto_micro_187250` — also saw repeated fallback logs from cublasLt: "Selected Algo 21 requires workspace size 536870912, allocation failed -> fallback to algo 37" but sometimes it still attempts 21 and does small alloc then free, thrash.
perf-bot: perf alert: regression +15% p50 latency on canary (commit b2f6a8e) for inference-2 route.
sarah: commit b2f6a8e is the batching heuristic PR. We should either: (A) limit batch packing for matmul shapes below a threshold, or (B) change kernel selector to penalize workspace algos for small matmuls, or (C) add a per-call workspace cache/arena to avoid deviceAlloc churn.
dmitri: I'd vote C + B. Arena avoids many small malloc/free ops; penalizing workspace-heavy algos avoids choosing 512MB workspace for a 64x128 input.
aj: quick mitigation: roll back aggressive packing for canary and add a knob to cap per-GEMM workspace to e.g., 4MB. Anyone object to a canary rollback?
maya: +1 rollback, will queue immediate canary revert. Also opening an issue with reproducer and attaching nsys and perfetto traces.
sarah: I'll prototype a cheap heuristic: if matmul bytes < 1MB, force algo candidates with ws==0. Should be a small change in kernel_selector.
dmitri: also add metrics: workspace_alloc_count and avg_ws_size to runtime metrics so we can alert earlier.
aj: created PR to rollback canary: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/commit/9c4a1e (revert b2f6a8e)
maya: pushed issue with logs and traces: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/issues/4129 — includes perfetto link and nsys artifacts.
perf-bot: note: schedule dedicated profiling run after rollback to confirm baseline.
maya: plan: rollback canary now, add workspace arena + kernel penalization in a follow-up (target EOD), add metric. Assigning tasks: aj -> revert rollout, sarah -> kernel_selector heuristic prototype, dmitri -> arena design, maya -> repro artifacts + microbench.
aj: started revert, will post when canary has switched.
dmitri: quick thought about arena: keep small-block pool and a single large reserved slab for >8MB requests to avoid fragmentation. Will draft design.
sarah: I'll add unit tests for selector to prefer ws==0 for <1MB matmuls.
maya: thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with nsys/perfetto links once revert completes.
aj: revert done on canary at 1872507600 — perf p50 dropped back to baseline on initial checks.
maya: verified traces show much fewer deviceAlloc calls. Closing urgent incident, will follow up on follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
